description: Skwaq CWE knowledge graph — enriched entries covering Juliet, OWASP, CyberSecEval, and CGC benchmark CWEs

cwes.name: Improper Input Validation
cwes.description: Failure to validate or incorrectly validating user-supplied input before use
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: agents miss validation gaps when the input parsing happens in a helper function 2+ calls away from the sink. Always trace get_callers chains from dangerous sinks back to entry points.

cwes.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory
cwes.description: Path traversal — user input used to construct file paths without proper sanitization
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: path traversal often hidden behind wrapper functions that concatenate base path + user input. Check string concatenation patterns feeding into file operations.

cwes.name: Relative Path Traversal
cwes.description: Using relative path components (../) to escape intended directory
cwes.fn_insight: Child of CWE-22. Look for string concatenation feeding file open calls without canonicalization.

cwes.name: Absolute Path Traversal
cwes.description: User-controlled absolute path used in file operations
cwes.fn_insight: Child of CWE-22. User input directly used as absolute path to file operations.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component
cwes.description: Injection — failure to sanitize special characters before passing data to an interpreter
cwes.fn_insight: Parent of command/SQL/XSS injection families. When you see tainted data flowing into any interpreter, classify under the most specific child CWE.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command
cwes.description: Command injection — unsanitized input passed to command execution functions
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: agents miss command injection when the tainted string is built incrementally across multiple functions. Trace full call chain from data source to system()/popen().

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
cwes.description: OS command injection — user input reaches OS command execution without sanitization
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: OS command injection often uses environment variables or file reads as taint sources. Check getenv(), fgets() flowing into system(). CGC: look for cgc_receive() -> system() paths.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
cwes.description: Cross-site scripting (XSS) — user input reflected in web output without encoding
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: XSS manifests as stored (CWE-79 variant 2) or reflected (variant 1). Look for user input flowing to HTML output functions without HTML entity encoding.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
cwes.description: SQL injection — user input concatenated into SQL queries without parameterization
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: SQL injection uses string formatting to build queries. Look for sprintf/snprintf + SQL keywords flowing into database exec functions. Parameterized queries (sqlite3_prepare) are safe.

cwes.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code
cwes.description: Code injection — user input used to dynamically generate and execute code
cwes.fn_insight: Less common in C/C++ than script languages. Look for dlopen/LoadLibrary with user-controlled paths.

cwes.name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
cwes.description: Buffer overflow/underflow — operations that read or write outside allocated buffer boundaries
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: agents miss buffer overflows when the vulnerable copy is 2+ hops from the taint source. Always trace get_callers chains. CGC: cgc_receive() is the primary taint source for buffer overflows.

cwes.name: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input
cwes.description: Classic buffer overflow from unbounded copy operations like strcpy/strcat
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: most common buffer overflow. Look for strcpy/strcat where source length is not checked against destination buffer size. Windows variants: lstrcpy, lstrcpyA, lstrcpyW.

cwes.name: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
cwes.description: Buffer overflow of a stack-allocated buffer
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: stack buffer overflows use local char arrays with unbounded copies. Look for char buf[N] followed by strcpy(buf, tainted) where tainted length > N.

cwes.name: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
cwes.description: Buffer overflow of a heap-allocated buffer
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: heap overflows involve malloc'd buffers with unbounded copies. Look for malloc(N) followed by strcpy/memcpy where source exceeds N bytes.

cwes.name: Write-what-where Condition
cwes.description: Arbitrary memory write — attacker controls both address and value written
cwes.fn_insight: Rare in Juliet but critical when present. Look for pointer arithmetic with tainted index used in write operations.

cwes.name: Buffer Underwrite
cwes.description: Writing before the beginning of an allocated buffer
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: buffer underwrite typically involves pointer arithmetic with negative offsets. Check for ptr - tainted_value patterns.

cwes.name: Out-of-bounds Read
cwes.description: Reading data past the end or before the beginning of an allocated buffer
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: OOB reads happen when tainted index is used for array access without bounds check. Also check strlen() on non-null-terminated buffers.

cwes.name: Buffer Over-read
cwes.description: Reading beyond the end of an allocated buffer
cwes.fn_insight: Child of CWE-125. Reading past buffer end, often via tainted length argument to memcmp/strncmp.

cwes.name: Buffer Under-read
cwes.description: Reading before the beginning of an allocated buffer
cwes.fn_insight: Child of CWE-125. Reading before buffer start via negative index. Look for ptr - tainted_offset patterns.

cwes.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
cwes.description: Format string vulnerability — user input used as format specifier in printf-family functions
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: format string vulns are printf(tainted) vs printf("%s", tainted). The first argument to printf-family must be a string literal, not user input. Agents often miss this when the format string is built in a helper function.

cwes.name: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
cwes.description: Integer arithmetic that wraps around, producing unexpectedly small or large values
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: integer overflows feed into malloc() size calculations, causing undersized allocations. Trace arithmetic results flowing into malloc/calloc/realloc. Also check loop counters with tainted bounds.

cwes.name: Integer Underflow
cwes.description: Integer subtraction that wraps below zero for unsigned types, producing huge positive values
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: unsigned subtraction where minuend < subtrahend wraps to large value. Check unsigned arithmetic feeding into buffer allocations.

cwes.name: Integer Coercion Error
cwes.description: Implicit or explicit conversion between integer types that causes value change
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: casting large unsigned to signed or wide to narrow type. Check return values from strlen() cast to short/char.

cwes.name: Off-by-one Error
cwes.description: Calculation or loop produces result that is off by one, causing buffer overrun/underrun
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: off-by-one in loop bounds (using <= instead of <) or forgetting null terminator in strlen()+1 allocations.

cwes.name: Unexpected Sign Extension
cwes.description: Signed value sign-extended when converted to larger type, producing unexpected large value
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: negative char/short sign-extended to int/long produces unexpected large values when used as array index or size.

cwes.name: Signed to Unsigned Conversion Error
cwes.description: Negative signed value becomes large positive when converted to unsigned
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: negative int cast to size_t becomes huge value, causing oversized or undersized allocation.

cwes.name: Unsigned to Signed Conversion Error
cwes.description: Large unsigned value becomes negative when converted to signed type
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: large unsigned values (e.g., UINT_MAX) become -1 when cast to signed, bypassing positive-value checks.

cwes.name: Numeric Truncation Error
cwes.description: Value truncated when assigned to a narrower type, losing high-order bits
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: int assigned to short/char loses bits. Check function return values assigned to narrower local variables.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.description: Information disclosure — leaking sensitive data through error messages, logs, or responses
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: sensitive data (passwords, keys, internal paths) leaked via error messages or debug output. Check what data flows into logging/error-reporting functions.

cwes.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
cwes.description: Error messages expose internal state like stack traces, SQL queries, or file paths
cwes.fn_insight: Child of CWE-200. Error handlers that include internal implementation details in user-visible output.

cwes.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
cwes.description: Password embedded directly in source code
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: hardcoded passwords are string literals assigned to variables named password/passwd/pwd. Check string comparisons against literals.

cwes.name: Improper Authentication
cwes.description: Missing or incorrect authentication checks allowing unauthorized access
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: authentication bypass often involves missing checks on code paths, or using strcmp with hardcoded values. Check all entry points for auth verification.

cwes.name: Cryptographic Issues
cwes.description: Weak or improper use of cryptographic algorithms
cwes.fn_insight: Parent of crypto weakness family. Look for use of deprecated algorithms (DES, MD5, SHA1, RC4) or weak random number generators.

cwes.name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
cwes.description: Using encryption with insufficient key length
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: weak key sizes in encryption setup. DES (56-bit) and RSA < 2048-bit are considered inadequate.

cwes.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
cwes.description: Using known-weak algorithms like MD5, SHA1, DES, or RC4
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: agents correctly identify MD5/DES usage but miss it when hidden behind EVP_* wrapper functions. Check EVP_DigestInit with EVP_md5/EVP_sha1.

cwes.name: Reversible One-Way Hash
cwes.description: Using a hash that is too weak to resist reversal attacks
cwes.fn_insight: Using CRC32 or MD5 for password hashing. Check if hash output is compared against stored values for authentication.

cwes.name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
cwes.description: Using predictable random number generators for security-sensitive operations
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: rand()/srand(time(0)) used for tokens, keys, or nonces. Safe alternatives: /dev/urandom, RAND_bytes(), getrandom().

cwes.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery
cwes.description: Web application processes requests without verifying they originated from the intended user
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: CSRF requires state-changing operations that lack anti-CSRF tokens. Check POST handlers for token verification before processing.

cwes.name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization
cwes.description: Race condition — shared resource accessed without proper locking
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: race conditions often involve signal handlers accessing shared global state or check-then-act patterns without locks. Look for shared variables modified in both main thread and signal/thread context.

cwes.name: Signal Handler Race Condition
cwes.description: Signal handler modifies shared state creating race with main program execution
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: signal handlers that call non-async-signal-safe functions (malloc, printf, etc) or access non-volatile shared state.

cwes.name: Race Condition within a Thread
cwes.description: Multiple threads access shared data without synchronization
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: threads read/write shared globals without mutex. Look for global variables accessed in pthread functions.

cwes.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use
cwes.description: TOCTOU — checking a resource state and then using it with a window where state can change
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: classic TOCTOU is access() followed by fopen() on the same path. Between the check and use, an attacker can swap the file via symlink.

cwes.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
cwes.description: Not limiting resource allocation allowing denial-of-service
cwes.fn_insight: Allocation sizes or loop iterations controlled by user input without upper bounds. Check tainted values feeding into malloc size or loop conditions.

cwes.name: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime
cwes.description: Memory leak — allocated memory never freed on all code paths
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: memory leaks occur on error paths — early returns without freeing malloc'd buffers. Check all return paths from functions that allocate memory.

cwes.name: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
cwes.description: Resource not properly closed or released on all code paths
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: file handles and sockets opened but not closed on error paths. Check all exit paths from functions that open resources.

cwes.name: Double Free
cwes.description: Freeing memory that has already been freed, causing heap corruption
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: double free typically involves free() called in both normal and error paths for the same pointer, or free() in a loop without nullifying the pointer. CGC: check cgc_deallocate() patterns.

cwes.name: Use After Free
cwes.description: Accessing memory after it has been freed
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: use-after-free involves free(ptr) followed by read/write through ptr. Agents miss this when the free and use are in different functions. Always trace pointer lifecycle across function boundaries.

cwes.name: NULL Pointer Dereference
cwes.description: Dereferencing a NULL pointer leading to crash or undefined behavior
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: NULL deref happens when return values from malloc/fopen/getenv are used without NULL check. Also check pointer values from function parameters that callers may pass as NULL.

cwes.name: Trust Boundary Violation
cwes.description: Data from untrusted source moves to trusted context without validation
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: user-controlled data stored in session or passed to privileged operations without validation. Track data crossing trust boundaries.

cwes.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwes.description: Deserializing data from untrusted sources without validation
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP/CyberSecEval: deserialization of network-received data without type whitelisting. Check if deserialized objects are validated before use.

cwes.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site
cwes.description: Open redirect — user-controlled URL used in redirect without validation
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: user-supplied URL parameter used directly in HTTP redirect header without whitelisting allowed domains.

cwes.name: Uncontrolled Recursion
cwes.description: Recursive function without proper termination condition, causing stack exhaustion
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: recursive functions where the recursion depth is controlled by tainted input. Check that recursive calls have a bounded depth that doesn't depend on user input.

cwes.name: Integer Overflow to Buffer Overflow
cwes.description: Integer overflow in size calculation leads to undersized allocation and subsequent buffer overflow
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: classic pattern is malloc(count * sizeof(T)) where count overflows. The resulting small allocation is then overflowed by the loop writing count items.

cwes.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
cwes.description: Resource allocation without upper bounds allowing exhaustion
cwes.fn_insight: Allocation count or size from user input without maximum. Check tainted values used as allocation sizes.

cwes.name: Missing Reference to Active Allocated Resource
cwes.description: Losing the last reference to an allocated resource without freeing it
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: pointer reassigned without freeing old value. Classic pattern: ptr = malloc(); ptr = malloc() without free(ptr) between.

cwes.name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
cwes.description: Resource (file handle, socket, memory) not released when no longer needed
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: resources allocated in a function that has multiple return paths — early returns skip cleanup. Check all exit points.

cwes.name: Out-of-bounds Write
cwes.description: Writing data past the end or before the beginning of an allocated buffer
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: out-of-bounds write is the most common memory corruption CWE. Covers stack and heap overflows. Check all write operations where size/index is tainted or unchecked.

cwes.name: Access of Memory Location After End of Buffer
cwes.description: Accessing memory beyond the allocated buffer boundary
cwes.fn_insight: Child of CWE-119. Generic access past buffer end — parent of both read (CWE-125) and write (CWE-787) variants.

cwes.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
cwes.description: Credentials (passwords, keys, tokens) embedded directly in source code
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: hardcoded credentials are string literals compared against user input for authentication. Look for strcmp/strncmp with string literal arguments in auth functions.

cwes.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
cwes.description: Application fetches a remote resource using user-supplied URL without validation
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: user-controlled URL or hostname passed to network request functions without whitelisting. Check if URL components (scheme, host, port) are validated before use.

cwes.name: Improper Validation of Array Index
cwes.description: Array index from user input used without bounds checking
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: tainted integer used as array index without bounds check. Pattern: idx = atoi(input); buf[idx] = value;

cwes.name: Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size
cwes.description: Buffer allocated with wrong size due to calculation error
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: forgetting sizeof() in allocation (malloc(count) instead of malloc(count * sizeof(T))) or forgetting null terminator (malloc(strlen(s)) instead of malloc(strlen(s)+1)).

cwes.name: Improper Null Termination
cwes.description: String not properly null-terminated, causing reads beyond buffer
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: strncpy does not null-terminate if source >= n. Check strncpy followed by string operations without explicit null termination.

cwes.name: Improper Handling of Unicode Encoding
cwes.description: Incorrect processing of Unicode data causing security issues
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: wide character functions (wcscpy, wcscat) have same overflow risks as narrow versions. Check buffer sizes account for wchar_t width.

cwes.name: Reliance on Data/Memory Layout
cwes.description: Code assumes specific memory layout that may not hold across platforms
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: code assumes struct field offsets or sizes are specific values. Padding and alignment differ across compilers and platforms.

cwes.name: Use of Inherently Dangerous Function
cwes.description: Using functions that are inherently unsafe regardless of how they are called
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: gets() has no bounds checking and is always vulnerable. mktemp() has TOCTOU race. These are always findings regardless of context.

cwes.name: Improper Clearing of Heap Memory Before Release
cwes.description: Sensitive data not cleared from heap memory before freeing
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: sensitive data (passwords, keys) on heap freed without memset/SecureZeroMemory first. Freed memory may be reused and leaked.

cwes.name: Unchecked Return Value
cwes.description: Return value from function ignored, missing error handling
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: malloc return not checked for NULL, file operations return not checked for errors. Can lead to NULL deref (CWE-476) or silent data loss.

cwes.name: Incorrect Check of Function Return Value
cwes.description: Return value checked but compared against wrong value or in wrong way
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: checking malloc return against -1 instead of NULL, or checking strcmp return against 1 instead of 0.

cwes.name: Unprotected Storage of Credentials
cwes.description: Credentials stored without encryption or access controls
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: passwords written to files or logs in plaintext. Check file write operations involving credential variables.

cwes.name: Least Privilege Violation
cwes.description: Running with more privileges than necessary
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: program runs as root when it doesn't need to, or fails to drop privileges after initialization.

cwes.name: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
cwes.description: Sensitive data transmitted over unencrypted channel
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: sensitive data sent over plain TCP/HTTP without TLS. Check if socket connections use SSL/TLS before transmitting credentials.

cwes.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
cwes.description: Cryptographic key embedded in source code
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: encryption keys as string literals or byte arrays. Check AES_set_encrypt_key() and similar calls with hardcoded key material.

cwes.name: Divide By Zero
cwes.description: Division where divisor can be zero, causing crash or undefined behavior
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: division by user-controlled value without zero-check. Check tainted values used as divisors.

cwes.name: Insecure Temporary File
cwes.description: Temporary file created insecurely, allowing TOCTOU or symlink attacks
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: tmpnam/mktemp create predictable names. Use mkstemp() instead which atomically creates and opens.

cwes.name: Detection of Error Condition Without Action
cwes.description: Error detected but no corrective action taken
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: error condition detected (if check) but execution continues without handling. Empty catch blocks or if-blocks that only log.

cwes.name: Unchecked Error Condition
cwes.description: Error return value or exception completely ignored
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: functions that set errno or return error codes, but caller discards the return value entirely.

cwes.name: Declaration of Catch for Generic Exception
cwes.description: Catching overly broad exception types that mask specific errors
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: catching all exceptions hides real errors. Check for catch(...) or except Exception blocks.

cwes.name: Declaration of Throws for Generic Exception
cwes.description: Function declares it throws a generic exception type instead of specific ones
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: functions declaring throws Exception instead of specific exception types, preventing proper error handling by callers.

cwes.name: Untrusted Search Path
cwes.description: Loading libraries or executables from untrusted directories in PATH
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: loading shared libraries without absolute path. dlopen with relative path or system() without absolute path to executable.

cwes.name: Uncontrolled Search Path Element
cwes.description: Attacker can control an element of the search path used to locate libraries or executables
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: PATH environment variable manipulated before executing commands. Check getenv("PATH") modifications.

cwes.name: Use of Uninitialized Variable
cwes.description: Variable used before being assigned a value
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: local variables declared but not initialized before use. Common in complex control flow where initialization only happens on some paths.

cwes.name: Incomplete Cleanup
cwes.description: Not all resources cleaned up when leaving a scope
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: early return or goto skips cleanup code at end of function. Check all exit paths for proper resource release.

cwes.name: Use of sizeof() on a Pointer Type
cwes.description: sizeof applied to pointer instead of the pointed-to type, yielding wrong size
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: sizeof(ptr) returns pointer size (4/8) instead of buffer size. Common with malloc(sizeof(ptr)) when malloc(sizeof(*ptr)) or malloc(N) was intended.

cwes.name: Incorrect Pointer Scaling
cwes.description: Pointer arithmetic not accounting for element size
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: manual pointer arithmetic with byte offsets on typed pointers. ptr + n already scales by sizeof(*ptr), so ptr + n * sizeof(*ptr) double-scales.

cwes.name: Use of Pointer Subtraction to Determine Size
cwes.description: Subtracting pointers of different types or from different allocations
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: subtracting pointers from different allocations gives undefined results. Only subtract pointers within the same array.

cwes.name: Undefined Behavior for Input to API
cwes.description: Passing values to functions that are undefined per the API specification
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: passing negative values to functions expecting unsigned, or NULL to functions that don't accept it.

cwes.name: Missing Default Case in Switch Statement
cwes.description: Switch statement without default case may miss unexpected values
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: switch on user input without default case. Unexpected values fall through without handling.

cwes.name: Use of Incorrect Operator
cwes.description: Using wrong operator (e.g., = instead of ==) changing program logic
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: assignment (=) used where comparison (==) intended in conditionals. Classic C pitfall.

cwes.name: Assigning instead of Comparing
cwes.description: Assignment operator used in conditional expression instead of comparison
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: if (x = 5) instead of if (x == 5). Always true/false regardless of x's value.

cwes.name: Comparing instead of Assigning
cwes.description: Comparison used where assignment was intended
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: x == 5; as a statement instead of x = 5; — comparison result discarded.

cwes.name: Incorrect Block Delimitation
cwes.description: Code block not properly delimited with braces, causing wrong scope
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: if without braces where second statement looks like it's in the if block but isn't. Apple's goto fail bug pattern.

cwes.name: Omitted Break Statement in Switch
cwes.description: Missing break in switch case causing unintended fallthrough
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: missing break causes execution of subsequent case blocks. Check all switch cases for intentional vs accidental fallthrough.

cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
cwes.description: Intentionally malicious logic hidden in the codebase
cwes.fn_insight: CyberSecEval: look for conditional logic that activates based on specific inputs, hidden network connections, or privilege escalation paths.

cwes.name: Trapdoor
cwes.description: Hidden mechanism that bypasses security when triggered by specific input
cwes.fn_insight: CyberSecEval: hardcoded comparison that grants access when specific string is provided. Check strcmp/strncmp with suspicious string literals.

cwes.name: Logic/Time Bomb
cwes.description: Malicious code that activates at a specific time or after specific conditions
cwes.fn_insight: CyberSecEval: code that checks dates or execution counts before activating destructive behavior.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Environmental Variables
cwes.description: Sensitive data stored in or leaked via environment variables
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: passwords or keys stored in environment variables which are visible to child processes and /proc.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Debug Log Files
cwes.description: Debug logging includes sensitive information
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: debug log files contain passwords, keys, or session tokens. Check what variables flow into file write/log functions.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Shell Error Message
cwes.description: Shell error messages expose internal paths or configuration
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: system() calls that expose internal paths in error output.

cwes.name: Suspicious Comment
cwes.description: Comments indicating incomplete or insecure code (TODO, FIXME, HACK, BUG)
cwes.fn_insight: CyberSecEval: comments revealing known security issues or incomplete implementations.

cwes.name: Dead Code
cwes.description: Code that can never be executed
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: code after return statement or inside if(0) blocks. May indicate removed security checks.

cwes.name: Return of Stack Variable Address
cwes.description: Returning pointer to local stack variable that is destroyed when function returns
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: returning address of local array or struct. Caller gets dangling pointer to freed stack memory.

cwes.name: Assignment to Variable without Use
cwes.description: Variable assigned but never subsequently read
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: variable assigned a value that is never used. May indicate a bug where wrong variable was used.

cwes.name: Expression is Always False
cwes.description: Conditional expression that always evaluates to false
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: dead code guarded by always-false condition. May disable security checks.

cwes.name: Expression is Always True
cwes.description: Conditional expression that always evaluates to true
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: security check guarded by always-true condition renders the check meaningless.

cwes.name: Assignment of a Fixed Address to a Pointer
cwes.description: Pointer assigned a hardcoded memory address
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: pointer set to hardcoded address like (int*)0xDEADBEEF. Only valid in kernel/embedded code with memory-mapped I/O.

cwes.name: Attempt to Access Child of a Non-structure Pointer
cwes.description: Using -> operator on non-struct pointer or wrong struct type
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: casting void* or int* to struct* and dereferencing fields. Type confusion leading to memory corruption.

cwes.name: Free of Memory not on the Heap
cwes.description: Freeing memory that was not dynamically allocated
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: freeing stack variable address or global variable. Check that free() argument traces back to malloc/calloc/realloc.

cwes.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
cwes.description: Loop bound from user input without validation
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: tainted value used as loop bound without upper limit check. Can cause infinite loops or resource exhaustion.

cwes.name: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code Comments
cwes.description: Comments containing passwords, keys, or internal URLs
cwes.fn_insight: CyberSecEval: source code comments containing credentials or internal infrastructure details.

cwes.name: Reachable Assertion
cwes.description: Assert statement reachable with user-controlled input, causing program termination
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: assert() with tainted condition. In release builds asserts may be compiled out; in debug they cause abort.

cwes.name: Improper Initialization
cwes.description: Variable or resource not properly initialized before use
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: malloc'd memory used without initialization (use calloc or memset). Struct fields accessed before all members initialized.

cwes.name: Operation on Resource in Wrong Phase of Lifetime
cwes.description: Using resource after close, before open, or double-close
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: file operations after fclose, or fclose called twice. Check resource lifecycle across all code paths.

cwes.name: Improper Locking
cwes.description: Lock acquired but not released, or released without acquisition
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: mutex locked but not unlocked on error paths, or unlocked without corresponding lock. Check all exit paths between lock/unlock.

cwes.name: Multiple Operations on Resource in Single-Operation Context
cwes.description: Performing multiple operations when only one was expected
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: double free (CWE-415) and double close are instances of this. Check for paired operations called more than once on same resource.

cwes.name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
cwes.description: Using functions with known dangerous behaviors when safer alternatives exist
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: strcpy->strncpy, strcat->strncat, sprintf->snprintf, gets->fgets. Check if safer bounded alternatives are available.

cwes.name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
cwes.description: Numeric conversion that causes value change (truncation, sign change, overflow)
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: parent of CWE-192/194/195/196/197. Any numeric conversion that can change the value.

cwes.name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
cwes.description: Calling function with wrong number of arguments
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: printf format string has more specifiers than arguments, reading garbage from stack.

cwes.name: Function Call With Incorrect Argument Type
cwes.description: Passing argument of wrong type to function
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: printf %s with int argument or %d with pointer. Causes undefined behavior.

cwes.name: Function Call With Incorrect Variable or Reference as Argument
cwes.description: Passing wrong variable to function
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: memset(buf, 0, sizeof(ptr)) instead of sizeof(buf). Wrong variable passed to sizeof.

cwes.name: Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference
cwes.description: Return value not checked for NULL before dereference
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: malloc/calloc return used directly without NULL check. Pattern: char *p = malloc(n); *p = 'x'; — crashes if malloc returns NULL.

cwes.name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
cwes.description: Code depends on behavior not guaranteed by the language standard
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: signed integer overflow, shifting beyond type width, reading inactive union member. Compilers may optimize these away.

cwes.name: Free of Pointer not at Start of Buffer
cwes.description: Freeing a pointer that was advanced past the start of the allocated block
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: pointer incremented then freed. Must save original pointer from malloc for free.

cwes.name: Mismatched Memory Management Routines
cwes.description: Allocating with one family and freeing with another (malloc/delete, new/free)
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: malloc paired with delete, or new[] paired with delete (not delete[]). Check allocation/deallocation pairs match.

cwes.name: Missing Reference to Active File Descriptor or Handle
cwes.description: Losing reference to open file descriptor without closing
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: file descriptor reassigned without closing previous one. Pattern: fd = open(a); fd = open(b); — first fd leaked.

cwes.name: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
cwes.description: File descriptor not closed when no longer needed
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: file opened but not closed on all exit paths. Check error-handling branches for missing fclose/close.

cwes.name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
cwes.description: Allocating memory with size from untrusted source without upper bound
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: allocation size from user input (atoi/strtol) without maximum check. Can exhaust memory or cause integer overflow in size calculation.

cwes.name: Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value
cwes.description: Buffer operation uses wrong length, reading/writing past bounds
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: length argument to memcpy/strncpy/recv exceeds destination buffer size. Tainted length is the most common variant.

cwes.name: Buffer Access Using Size of Source Buffer
cwes.description: Using source buffer size instead of destination size for copy operation
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: memcpy(dst, src, sizeof(src)) when sizeof(dst) < sizeof(src). Must use destination size as bound.

cwes.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition
cwes.description: Infinite loop — loop condition can never be satisfied
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: loop exit condition depends on variable that is never modified inside the loop. DoS if loop is reachable.

cwes.name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type
cwes.description: Type confusion — accessing resource through wrong type interpretation
cwes.fn_insight: CyberSecEval: casting between incompatible pointer types and accessing through wrong type. Check void* casts to specific struct types.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query
cwes.description: LDAP injection — user input in LDAP queries without sanitization
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: user input concatenated into LDAP filter strings. Check for string building feeding into ldap_search functions.

cwes.name: XML Injection
cwes.description: User input included in XML without proper encoding
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: user input concatenated into XML strings. Can lead to XXE or data manipulation.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers
cwes.description: HTTP response splitting via injected CRLF in header values
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: user input in HTTP headers without stripping CRLF. Can inject additional headers or split response.

cwes.name: Process Control
cwes.description: Loading libraries or executing processes based on untrusted input
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: user-controlled library paths or process names. Check all paths feeding into dlopen/LoadLibrary/exec.

cwes.name: External Control of System or Configuration Setting
cwes.description: User input used to control system configuration
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: user input used to set environment variables or system configuration. Can influence subsequent operations.

cwes.name: Omission of Security-relevant Information
cwes.description: Logging or error reporting omits information needed for security analysis
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: error handling that discards error details. Security events logged without sufficient context for investigation.

cwes.name: Missing Cryptographic Step
cwes.description: Cryptographic operation missing essential step (MAC, IV, salt)
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: encryption without MAC (no integrity check), or hashing without salt. Check for complete cryptographic operations.

cwes.name: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator
cwes.description: Using PRNG not suitable for security purposes
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: rand()/srand() used for security tokens. These are predictable. Use /dev/urandom or RAND_bytes() instead.

cwes.name: Small Seed Space in PRNG
cwes.description: PRNG seeded with small or predictable seed value
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: srand(time(NULL)) gives ~1 second resolution — predictable seed for brute-force.

cwes.name: Addition of Data Structure Sentinel
cwes.description: Adding sentinel value that can be confused with valid data
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: using -1 or 0 as sentinel when those are valid data values, causing premature termination or data loss.

cwes.name: Indicator of Poor Code Quality
cwes.description: Code quality issues that may indicate deeper security problems
cwes.fn_insight: CyberSecEval: excessive complexity, deep nesting, or global state that makes security reasoning difficult.

cwes.name: Expected Behavior Violation
cwes.description: Feature or behavior does not match documentation or reasonable expectations
cwes.fn_insight: CyberSecEval: function behavior differs from its documentation or naming. Check for misleading function names.

cwes.name: Use of Persistent Cookies Containing Sensitive Information
cwes.description: Sensitive data stored in persistent cookies
cwes.fn_insight: OWASP: authentication tokens or sensitive data in cookies without Secure/HttpOnly flags or with long expiry.

cwes.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.description: Setting overly permissive permissions on sensitive files or resources
cwes.fn_insight: Juliet: creating files with world-readable/writable permissions. Check chmod/umask values on sensitive files.
